title: NCH Filing Procedure & Grievance Registration
text: Consumers can register their grievances against e-commerce companies with the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) through the Integrated Grievance Redress Mechanism (INGRAM) portal, mobile app, WhatsApp, SMS, or by calling Toll-Free Number 1915 or 1800-11-4000. NCH acts as a pre-litigation alternate dispute resolution mechanism forwarding the grievance directly to registered convergence partner companies for speedy resolution.

title: NCH Evidence Documentation Checklist for Online Shopping
text: To process an e-commerce grievance effectively, the consumer should furnish the following supporting documents: 1. Tax invoice / purchase receipt showing seller name and price paid; 2. Order confirmation email/SMS with Order ID and date; 3. Proof of payment (UPI transaction ID, bank statement snippet, payment gateway receipt); 4. Screenshots of customer care chat/email tickets and complaint tracking numbers; 5. Unboxing video or clear defect photos in case of wrong, damaged, or counterfeit products; 6. Bank account statement confirming non-receipt of refund amount beyond promised turnaround time (TAT).

title: NCH Resolution Timelines and Consumer Commission Escalation
text: E-commerce convergence partner companies are expected to respond to grievances registered via NCH within a reasonable timeframe (typically 15 to 30 days). If the grievance remains unresolved, rejected without justification, or if the company fails to respond, the consumer may escalate the dispute by filing a formal consumer complaint before the competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 via the e-Daakhil electronic filing portal (edaakhil.nic.in).

title: NCH FAQ — Delayed and Unprocessed E-Commerce Refunds
text: If a refund was initiated by an e-commerce platform but not credited to the consumer's bank account or original payment method within the standard turnaround time (typically 5-7 business days for UPI/cards), the consumer should first obtain the ARN (Acquirer Reference Number) or transaction reference from the platform. If the platform fails to provide ARN or the bank confirms no credit, the consumer is entitled to register a grievance for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, claiming immediate refund along with compensation for delay.
